source: Compiled from Visual Capitalist ("Mapping the World's Key Maritime Choke Points"), Mappr ("Mapped: The World's Most Important Straits and Chokepoints"), and US EIA world oil transit chokepoint reporting.
note: Ranked by a blend of oil-transit volume, share of world trade, and vessel-traffic count -- not a single official ranking, since no one metric captures 'importance' the same way across all ten.

chokepoints.name: Strait of Malacca
chokepoints.stat: ~1/4 of all globally traded goods; the main artery for East Asia's oil imports.
chokepoints.note: Between Sumatra and the Malay Peninsula. As little as ~1.5 nautical miles wide at its narrowest, and the single busiest maritime chokepoint on Earth.

chokepoints.name: Strait of Hormuz
chokepoints.stat: ~20 million barrels of oil per day -- roughly a fifth of global oil supply.
chokepoints.note: Between the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman. The world's most important oil chokepoint, and one of its most geopolitically sensitive.

chokepoints.name: Suez Canal
chokepoints.stat: 12-15% of world trade; ~19,000 vessel transits and roughly 1 billion tons of cargo a year.
chokepoints.note: Connects the Mediterranean to the Red Sea, cutting ~7 days off the alternative route around Africa.

chokepoints.name: Panama Canal
chokepoints.stat: ~5% of world trade; saves ships over 8,000 nautical miles versus rounding South America.
chokepoints.note: Connects the Atlantic and Pacific via a lock system; critical for Asia-US East Coast trade.

chokepoints.name: Bab-el-Mandeb Strait
chokepoints.stat: ~8.7 million barrels of oil per day.
chokepoints.note: Between Yemen and Djibouti/Eritrea, linking the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden -- the southern gateway that feeds the Suez Canal.

chokepoints.name: Strait of Dover / English Channel
chokepoints.stat: 400+ vessels a day -- the busiest strait in the world by ship count.
chokepoints.note: Between England and France, linking the North Sea to the Atlantic. As narrow as ~33 km wide.

chokepoints.name: Strait of Gibraltar
chokepoints.note: Between Spain and Morocco -- the only sea gateway between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean.

chokepoints.name: Bosphorus
chokepoints.stat: Sole route for Russian and Ukrainian oil and grain exports from the Black Sea.
chokepoints.note: Runs through Istanbul, as narrow as ~700 meters -- one of the narrowest and most heavily trafficked straits in the world.

chokepoints.name: Danish Straits (Great Belt)
chokepoints.stat: Carries the bulk of Russia's Baltic oil exports.
chokepoints.note: The main deep-water passage linking the Baltic Sea to the North Sea, between the Danish islands.

chokepoints.name: Taiwan Strait
chokepoints.stat: ~1/5 of global maritime trade transits this corridor.
chokepoints.note: Between Taiwan and mainland China -- among the most geopolitically sensitive shipping corridors in the world.
